The fifth criterion

The checks read together

Nine of the {{n_checks_word}} checks reduce a sequence to one feature and ask whether that feature alone separates the classes. The fifth criterion asks something the {{n_checks_word}} cannot answer between them: hand a model all of those same features at once — length, GC, mononucleotide and dinucleotide content, and the two per-position profiles — and score it on a held-out split. Nothing is added that the checks do not already look at. The only change is that they are read jointly rather than one at a time.

Over the {{n_joint_scored}} datasets a held-out split could be scored on, the median is {{median_joint_auroc}}, and {{n_joint_over_0_8}} reach 0.80 or more. The criterion cuts at 0.80, which is that median.

Two differences from every other number on this site are worth holding on to. It is measured on a held-out split, not on the reference split everything else is measured on, because a model fitted on the training pool and scored there would report how well it memorised. And it is still a lower bound, for the same reason a probe AUROC is: these are six fixed feature blocks, and a learned model has access to feature classes none of them spans.

{{n_joint_lower_bound}} of the {{n_joint_scored}} joint figures are lower bounds, not point values: the position window had to be capped, or the training pool subsampled. Both can only move the number down, so a dataset admitted for sitting under the ceiling may in fact sit above it. Every joint figure on this site that is a lower bound says so where it is shown.

{{joint_rows}}
The {{n_clean_but_joint_word}} datasets no check returned Fail on, which the same checks’ features recovered when read together. These are the datasets step 5 removed and no earlier step did.
Dataset Task category Strongest single feature All features together Scored on

This is the clearest thing this run has to say about what a Pass is worth. On every dataset in that table each of the {{n_checks_word}} checks returned Pass or Warning and none returned Fail; the features those checks are built from still recover the label. A row where the left figure is near 0.50 and the right is near 1.00 is not a check that misfired — each check answered the narrow question it was asked. It is the whole reason a flag bounds separability from below and never from above.

One consequence is recorded rather than smoothed over. RNA Processing Prediction has no eligible dataset anywhere in this corpus: one of its 11 audited datasets had no Fail on any check, and it does not clear the joint ceiling. So the Core Set spans six task categories and not seven, and the absent one is a finding about the corpus rather than a gap in the selection.

A Core Set member can still carry a Warning: the criteria screen for Fail. The strongest probe on a member still reaches an AUROC worth reading, and the joint column still reaches higher than it — both are there so they can be read.
